profile.campus: The Dalles, Wasco County, Oregon (Google's original self-built data center campus)
profile.address: Riverfront Trail, Google Taylor Lake Data Center, The Dalles, Wasco County, Oregon, 97058
profile.reading:
This building belongs to Google's Taylor Lake data center, a distinct, newer campus from the original 2006 West 2nd Street site though both sit within The Dalles, Wasco County. Data Center Dynamics reported Google opened phase one of the Taylor Lake facility in 2018, describing it as a two-story, roughly 164,000-square-foot building representing only the first stage of a larger planned project, built at a reported cost of around $600 million. Local coverage from KTVZ and the Columbia Gorge News described a ribbon-cutting event in March 2018 attended by Google and Wasco County officials, with construction at that phase employing more than 1,000 workers and the completed building expected to support roughly 50 permanent jobs, while a subsequent phase was projected to need an additional 750 temporary construction workers. Google's own data center locations page for Oregon reports the state total, more than $7 billion invested since 2006, covering both the West 2nd Street and Taylor Lake campuses together rather than breaking the figure out per site. Google has not published Taylor Lake's current total square footage following later expansion phases, nor its MW power capacity, consistent with the company's general practice of not disclosing per-building operating details. This registry treats the Taylor Lake buildings as a separate facility cluster from the original West 2nd Street campus given their different names, construction timeline, and reported investment figures, while noting both share the same Wasco County, Oregon jurisdiction and Google as operator.

Wasco County's enterprise zone agreement with Google, renewed as each new building at both the West 2nd Street and Taylor Lake campuses comes online, has abated local property taxes on the investment for set terms in exchange for the jobs and payroll Google commits to; county officials have pointed to that structure, alongside Oregon's lack of a state sales tax, as a material reason Google kept expanding in The Dalles rather than concentrating solely in newer data center markets.

reading.body:
Google Taylor Lake is a distinct newer campus from Google's original 2006 Dalles site, opened in phases beginning 2018 as a reported $600 million investment. The operator has not published power capacity or current total square footage for Taylor Lake following its expansion phases beyond the first building, which was a two-story, roughly 164,000-square-foot structure completed in 2018. Without a published megawatt figure, Taylor Lake's contribution to Oregon's AI infrastructure capacity cannot be directly calculated, placing it among the 125 facilities in Oregon with no disclosed operating power.

Oregon has 133 mapped data center facilities but only 8 publish power capacity figures, for a state total of 156.6 MW. Taylor Lake is not among the eight publishers and ranks ninth by published megawatt if included in state rankings, meaning it sits behind published facilities but its actual capacity relative to others in Oregon is unknown. The state's lack of sales tax and Wasco County's enterprise zone property tax abatement on Google's investment have been cited by local officials as material reasons Google expanded at The Dalles rather than concentrating in newer markets, a structure renewed as each new building opens.

The binding constraint on assessing Taylor Lake's role in AI scaling is the absence of any operator disclosure of its power draw or hardware count. Until Google publishes those figures, this campus remains operationally invisible to capacity planning, despite being Google's second-largest investment site in North America and almost certainly substantial by absolute megawatt measure.
